direction.tooltip: Whether to append audio2 after or before audio1.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

CLIPTextEncode.name: CLIPTextEncode
CLIPTextEncode.description: Encodes a text prompt using a CLIP model into an embedding that can be used to guide the diffusion model towards generating specific images.
output_tooltips: A conditioning containing the embedded text used to guide the diffusion model.

ckpt_name.tooltip: The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.

CheckpointLoaderSimple.name: CheckpointLoaderSimple
CheckpointLoaderSimple.description: Loads a diffusion model checkpoint, diffusion models are used to denoise latents.
output_tooltips: The model used for denoising latents.
The CLIP model used for encoding text prompts.
The VAE model used for encoding and decoding images to and from latent space.

image_target.tooltip: Image(s) to apply the color transform to.

image_ref.tooltip: Reference image(s) to match colors to.

source_stats.tooltip: per_frame: each frame matched to image_ref individually. uniform: pool stats across all source frames as baseline, match to image_ref. target_frame: use one chosen frame as the baseline for the transform to image_ref, applied uniformly to all frames (preserves relative differences)

target_index.tooltip: Frame index used as the source baseline for computing the transform to image_ref

ColorTransfer.name: ColorTransfer
ColorTransfer.description: Match the colors of one image to another using various algorithms.

videos.tooltip: Video segments to concatenate in input order.

codec.tooltip: Codec used to encode videos tensors. Auto uses H.264; already encoded videos remain unchanged.

complete_audio.tooltip: Optional complete soundtrack for the concatenated video. Overrides audio carried by the input videos.

output_tooltips: The concatenated video.
ConcatenateVideo.name: ConcatenateVideo
ConcatenateVideo.description: Concatenates videos in order without decoding compatible encoded inputs.

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit for sRGB and 10-bit for HDR. Explicit 8-bit and 10-bit choices are independent of colorspace.

color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

codec.tooltip: Optionally encode the video immediately. None keeps the images in tensor form; Auto uses H.264.

resolution.tooltip:
Resolution the model runs at (longest side, multiple of 14).
Lower = faster / less VRAM.
Higher = more detail.
Output is upsampled back to the original size.

resize_method.tooltip:
upper_bound_resize: scale so the longest side = resolution (caps memory, default).
lower_bound_resize: scale so the shortest side = resolution (preserves more detail on tall/wide images, uses more memory).

mode.tooltip:
mono: single view image (works with any model variant).
multiview: all images processed together for geometric consistency + camera pose (for Small/Base models only).

ref_view_strategy.tooltip:
Which view acts as the geometric anchor.
- saddle_balanced: the view most 'average' across all others (best general choice).
- saddle_sim_range: the view most visually distinct from the others.
- first / middle: fixed positional picks.

pose_method.tooltip:
How the camera field-of-view is estimated (for Small/Base models only).
- cam_dec: learned from image features.
- ray_pose: derived geometrically from the model's 3D ray output.
Affects perspective correctness of the 3D output. Try both if results look distorted.

output_tooltips:
Dictionary of non-normalized tensors.
Always has the keys: depth, image, mode.
Optional keys: sky (for Mono/Metric), confidence (for Small/Base), extrinsics + intrinsics (for multi-view).
DA3Inference.name: DA3Inference
DA3Inference.description: Run Depth Anything 3 on an image. In multi-view mode each image is treated as a separate view of the same scene.

output.tooltip:
- depth: normalised greyscale depth image.
- depth_colored: depth mapped through the Turbo colormap.
- sky_mask: sky probability in [0, 1] (for Mono/Metric models only).
- confidence: normalised depth confidence (for Small/Base models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

normalization.tooltip:
- v2_style: mean/std normalisation for perceptually balanced results (default).
- min_max: stretches the full depth range to [0, 1] for maximum contrast.
- raw: no scaling,preserves metric units for Metric model.

apply_sky_clip.tooltip: Clip sky-region depth to the 99th percentile of foreground depth before normalisation. Requires a sky key in the da3_geometry input (for Mono/Metric models only).

colored.tooltip: Apply the Turbo colormap to the sky mask.
Apply the Turbo colormap to the confidence map.

DA3Render.name: DA3Render
DA3Render.description: Render a depth map, confidence map, or sky mask from Depth Anything 3 geometry data.

GetImageSize.name: GetImageSize
GetImageSize.description: Returns the width, height, and batch size of the image.

video.tooltip: The video to extract components from.

GetVideoComponents.name: GetVideoComponents
GetVideoComponents.description: Extracts video frames, audio, frame rate, bit depth, and color space.

GrowMaskWithBlur.name: GrowMaskWithBlur
GrowMaskWithBlur.description:
# GrowMaskWithBlur
- mask: Input mask or mask batch
- expand: Expand or contract mask or mask batch by a given amount
- incremental_expandrate: increase expand rate by a given amount per frame
- tapered_corners: use tapered corners
- flip_input: flip input mask
- blur_radius: value higher than 0 will blur the mask
- lerp_alpha: alpha value for interpolation between frames
- decay_factor: decay value for interpolation between frames
- fill_holes: fill holes in the mask (slow)

ImageStitch.name: ImageStitch
ImageStitch.description:
Stitches image2 to image1 in the specified direction.
If image2 is not provided, returns image1 unchanged.
Optional spacing can be added between images.

model.tooltip: The model used for denoising the input latent.

seed.tooltip: The random seed used for creating the noise.

steps.tooltip: The number of steps used in the denoising process.

cfg.tooltip: The Classifier-Free Guidance scale balances creativity and adherence to the prompt. Higher values result in images more closely matching the prompt however too high values will negatively impact quality.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

positive.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to include in the image.

negative.tooltip: The conditioning describing the attributes you want to exclude from the image.

denoise.tooltip: The amount of denoising applied, lower values will maintain the structure of the initial image allowing for image to image sampling.

KSampler.name: KSampler
KSampler.description: Uses the provided model, positive and negative conditioning to denoise the latent image.
output_tooltips: The denoised latent.

Krea2AnyPaintEncode.name: Krea2AnyPaintEncode
Krea2AnyPaintEncode.description: Encode the full-canvas semantic reference and create a standard Comfy latent/noise_mask pair. KSampler performs timestep-matched known-region replacement; no final source composite is used.

Krea2AnyPaintModelPatch.name: Krea2AnyPaintModelPatch
Krea2AnyPaintModelPatch.description: Register the semantic reference over the complete target canvas and cache its isolated K/V once per sampling run. Place after Load LoRA.

Krea2AnyPaintPrepare.name: Krea2AnyPaintPrepare
Krea2AnyPaintPrepare.description: Place the source without resizing it. Padding and white mask pixels are generated; black mask pixels are preserved. The source image's Mask Editor output can be connected directly to generated_mask.

image_b.tooltip: 2nd reference (subject) for multi-ref LoRAs; vision blocks in training order: scene, subject

grounding_px.tooltip: cap longest side fed to Qwen3-VL; 0 = native

system_prompt.tooltip: advanced (optional): override the grounding system prompt (empty = training default). Steers what the vision encoder attends to, e.g. facial identity detail.

Krea2EditGroundedEncode.name: Krea2EditGroundedEncode
Krea2EditGroundedEncode.description: Encodes the edit instruction grounded on the source image (training-matched semantic path).

source_latent_b.tooltip: 2nd reference (subject photo) for multi-ref LoRAs -> RoPE frame=2, training-matched order: scene first, subject second

ref_boost.tooltip: reference-fidelity dial: multiplies target->reference attention. Applies to the LAST ref (= the subject in two-ref workflows, the only ref in single-ref). 1.0 = off, >1 pulls harder toward the reference's appearance, <1 loosens. Optimal value is model-specific

ref_boost_a.tooltip: same dial for the FIRST ref (= the scene in two-ref workflows). No effect in single-ref workflows. 1.0 = off

fit_mode.tooltip: how an image source fits a mismatched output aspect ratio (needs vae + source_image connected): fit = resample the source to the target grid at a centered offset — matches how this model was trained (default, use this); crop (legacy) = center-crop to the target AR then resize (v1/v1.1 geometry, only for older weights)

ref_boost_mask.tooltip: optional region on the (last) reference to boost, e.g. the face; empty = whole reference

vae.tooltip: RECOMMENDED with source_image: enables the blur-proof pixel-space path (crop+resize in pixels, encode internally) — immune to input/output resolution mismatches

source_image.tooltip: source as IMAGE (with vae connected): overrides source_latent with exact pixel-space fitting — fixes blurry results from mismatched resolutions

target_latent.tooltip: RECOMMENDED with vae + source_image: wire the SAME latent you feed KSampler.latent_image. Lets the node VAE-encode the source here, before sampling starts, instead of on the first step — otherwise the VAE is pulled onto the GPU mid-sampling and can evict part of the diffusion model, slowing every remaining step on VRAM-tight setups

Krea2EditModelPatch.name: Krea2EditModelPatch
Krea2EditModelPatch.description: Adds the krea2_edit in-context source-preservation path (source latent as frame=1 tokens) to a Krea2 model.

LTXVConcatAVLatent.name: LTXVConcatAVLatent
LTXVConcatAVLatent.description: Merge a video latent and an audio latent into a joint AV latent (any AV model, e.g. LTXV or MiniMax H3).

LTXVSeparateAVLatent.name: LTXVSeparateAVLatent
LTXVSeparateAVLatent.description: Split a joint AV latent into its video and audio latents (any AV model, e.g. LTXV or MiniMax H3).

bg_removal_name.tooltip: The model used to remove backgrounds from images

LoraLoaderModelOnly.description: This LoRAs loader is used to modify the diffusion model, altering the way in which latents are denoised such as applying styles. Multiple LoRA nodes can be linked together.
output_tooltips: The modified diffusion model.
The modified CLIP model.

mask.tooltip: Latent-resolution masks, one per latent frame.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the strongest value in each token block paints the whole block, matching how the model reads the mask. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal expansion (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

frames.tooltip: Pixel frame count to paint. 0 uses the count the compression grid implies for the incoming latent frames. Set it explicitly to match a source video that is off the model's frame grid.

vae.tooltip: The VAE whose latents this mask matches. Required when compression is auto.

output_tooltips: Pixel-space masks, one per frame.
MVEx_LatentMaskToMask.name: MVEx_LatentMaskToMask
MVEx_LatentMaskToMask.description: Expands a latent-resolution mask back to pixel resolution for visualization or testing. Each latent frame paints every pixel frame in its group and each token block paints as one value, so detail collapsed by the latent reduction stays collapsed.

masks.tooltip: Mask batch to clean, one mask per frame.

threshold.tooltip: Mask values above this count as subject when finding blobs.

method.tooltip: shrink_grow: shrinks the mask so thin specks vanish, then restores the surviving blobs' exact shapes. components: drops blobs that are both small and short-lived.

shrink.tooltip: Shrink distance in pixels. Blobs thinner than about twice this are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Surviving blobs must also persist at least this many frames. 1 disables the temporal check.

min_pixels.tooltip: Blobs whose largest single-frame area is below this many pixels are removed.

min_frames.tooltip: Small blobs must persist at least this many frames to survive.

edge_grow.tooltip: Grow kept regions by this many pixels so the subject's soft edges are preserved.

output_tooltips: Cleaned masks, same size and soft values as the input.
MVEx_MaskCleanup.name: MVEx_MaskCleanup
MVEx_MaskCleanup.description: Removes specks and brief flickering blobs from a video mask batch while keeping the real subject, including its soft edges.

compression.tooltip: auto: read the compression geometry from the connected VAE, including the exact frame cycle and 2x2 token grid of chunked models like MiniMax H3. manual: enter it directly.

spatial.tooltip: Pixels per latent pixel on each axis.

token_spatial.tooltip: Latent pixels per model token on each axis; the mask is unified over each token block. 2 for MiniMax H3, 1 for models that read the mask per latent pixel.

head_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in the model's leading frame group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX. 0 when the model has no leading group.

head_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by the leading group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

chunk_frames.tooltip: Pixel frames in each repeating group after the leading group. 4 for Wan and Hunyuan, 8 for LTX. 1 disables temporal reduction (image models).

chunk_latents.tooltip: Latent frames produced by each repeating group. 1 for Wan, Hunyuan and LTX.

frames_per_latent.tooltip: Exact pixel frames covered by each latent frame, comma-separated, repeating from the first frame. Overrides the grid above when set. 1,4,4,4,4 with spatial 16 for MiniMax H3. For frame counts off the model's grid, use auto.

spatial_method.tooltip: How a block of pixels reduces to one latent pixel. max marks the cell if any pixel is masked, min only if all are.

temporal_method.tooltip: How a group of frames reduces to one latent frame. max marks the frame if any grouped frame is masked.

grow_spatial.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many pixels before reduction.

grow_temporal.tooltip: Grow (+) or shrink (-) the mask this many frames before reduction.

grow_temp_mode.tooltip: Directionality of grow_temporal: both: earlier and later frames. forward: later frames only. backward: earlier frames only. chunks: whole encoder chunks instead of frames, so the mask only changes at chunk boundaries. (requires a chunked encoder like H3 VAE).

vae.tooltip: The VAE used to encode the latents this mask will be applied to. Required when compression is auto.

output_tooltips: Latent-resolution mask for Set Latent Noise Mask.
MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace.name: MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace
MVEx_MaskToLatentSpace.description: Reduces a pixel-space mask batch to latent resolution using the VAE's spatial and temporal compression, aligned to causal video VAE frame grouping and to the model's token grid (2x2 latent pixels for MiniMax H3). Feed the result to Set Latent Noise Mask.

masks.tooltip: Subject masks, one per frame. Clean them first (Mask Cleanup) if the segmentation is noisy.

mode.tooltip: In order of increasing complexity. combined: one static crop with padding around the subject's whole travel. tracked: a constant-size crop that stays still until the subject would leave it, then moves as little as possible. zoomed: the crop also follows the subject's size, planned over the whole clip, every crop resampled to a fixed output resolution.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's combined extent across all frames: 1.5 leaves a third of the crop as margin around the whole travel. 1.0 hugs the travel exactly. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78), reached by growing the smaller dimension. 0 sizes width and height from the mask's whole travel.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size or movement; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop runs larger so it can move less. tightness: the crop stays as small as the padding allows and moves as much as needed instead.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Crop shape as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and size for this clip.

seamless_loop.tooltip: Plan the crop path so the last frame wraps seamlessly into the first. Only for clips that genuinely repeat.

crop_scale.tooltip: Crop size as a multiple of the subject's size: 1.5 keeps the subject at two thirds of the crop with the rest as padding, so the subject holds a constant share of the output at any resolution. 1.0 crops tight, leaving no padding for the padding setting to keep; 4.0 surrounds the subject with three times its own size. At 0 cropping is skipped and the whole frame passes through, resized to the divisible_by grid when needed.

padding.tooltip: How firmly the crop_scale padding is kept. guaranteed: never less than promised on any frame, whatever it costs in size, movement, or rescaling; only the image edge can break it, and mask noise counts as subject, so clean the masks first. firm: at least 70% is always kept, the rest yields briefly during fast motion. flexible: padding yields first whenever keeping it would cost stillness or tightness.

prefer.tooltip: What pays for keeping the padding when the subject moves. stillness: the crop moves and rescales as little as possible, running larger instead. tightness: the crop and the output resolution stay as small as the padding allows, moving and rescaling as much as needed instead.

pad_surplus_tol.tooltip: Extra padding (a crop bigger than needed) lasting shorter than this many frames is kept rather than trimmed, riding out occlusions and dips at a steady size. At 1 the crop follows every size change tightly; very high holds one constant size for the whole clip.

zoom_step.tooltip: Whether crop size changes smoothly or snaps to discrete zoom levels this ratio apart. At 1.0 size changes continuously; at 2.0 every zoom level doubles the previous one.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Shape of every crop and of the output resolution, as width divided by height (e.g. 1.78). 0 lets the planner choose the shape that best balances padding, stillness, and rescaling for this clip. Output size is automatic: the largest crop stays at 1:1 pixel scale.

seamless_loop.tooltip: Plan crop position and size so the last frame wraps seamlessly into the first. Only for clips that genuinely repeat.

divisible_by.tooltip: Crop width and height are rounded up to a multiple of this. Match the model's resolution requirement.

upscale_megapixels.tooltip: Upscale the cropped images/masks to this many megapixels, on the divisible_by grid. Set to 0.0 to disable. (Use a negative value to allow scaling down as well as up.)

resize_method.tooltip: Resampling filter used when a crop is resized (masks are unaffected). auto uses bicubic to enlarge and lanczos to shrink.

output_tooltips: Constant-size crops, one per frame.
The input masks cropped to the same boxes. Feed to Subject Uncrop to confine the paste to the subject.
One box per frame, for Subject Uncrop.
Summary of the plan: chosen shape, box sizes, movement, and how much of the padding promise was kept.
MVEx_SubjectCrop.name: MVEx_SubjectCrop
MVEx_SubjectCrop.description: Crops a region around the masked subject from every frame, sized so the whole batch stacks into one tensor. Position, size, and shape are chosen together over the whole clip, so the crop holds still through mask jitter and follows only sustained motion.

feather.tooltip: Blend width in pixels, feathered inward from the crop border. Sides touching the image edge are not feathered.

resize_method.tooltip: Resampling filter used when a crop is resized (masks are unaffected). auto uses bicubic to enlarge and lanczos to shrink.

bboxes.tooltip: Boxes from Subject Crop, one per frame. A single box or single frame is applied to every frame; extra boxes within a frame are ignored. When inputs disagree on frame count, extra frames are dropped. When not connected, the crops are treated as covering the whole frame.

cropped_masks.tooltip: Confines the paste to the mask, one per crop at any resolution. A single mask is applied to every frame. Used exactly as given; pre-blur the mask for a soft edge.

output_tooltips: Original frames with the crops blended back in.
MVEx_SubjectUncrop.name: MVEx_SubjectUncrop
MVEx_SubjectUncrop.description: Pastes processed crops back into the original frames with a feathered border, optionally confined by a mask. The paste is pixel-exact when the crop size was not changed.

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to anchor the image or the clip's first frame at. Negative values are counted from the end of the video.

vae.tooltip: Video VAE, needed when an image is connected.

audio_vae.tooltip: Audio VAE, needed when an audio is connected.

image.tooltip: Image or video frames to anchor. Multi-frame batches are anchored as a clip and cropped down to the model's valid clip lengths: 5, 22, 39... (17k + 5) frames. Batches shorter than 5 frames use only the first image.

audio.tooltip: Soundtrack to anchor starting at the same frame index, cropped to the video's remaining duration.

MiniMaxH3AddGuide.name: MiniMaxH3AddGuide
MiniMaxH3AddGuide.description: Anchor an image, a short clip, audio, or a clip with its soundtrack at any frame of a MiniMax H3 video. Chain several nodes to anchor several frames.

source_video.tooltip: Video behind the mask; only read when a mask is given.

MiniMaxH3FunControlNetApply.name: MiniMaxH3FunControlNetApply
MiniMaxH3FunControlNetApply.description: Apply a MiniMax H3 Fun ControlNet to a text-to-video model as a model patch.

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, snapped up to the model's 17k+5 grid (124 = ~5s; trained range is ~124-362, longer is untested)

pad_clips.tooltip: 17-frame clips of wrapped context added on each side of the loop. Each clip adds sampling time.

views.tooltip: 2 also samples the loop rotated by half and takes the audio around the loop point from it. Fixes garbled audio there; about 1.8x sampling time. Not usable with the Fun ControlNet.

MiniMaxH3Loop.name: MiniMaxH3Loop
MiniMaxH3Loop.description: Generate a seamless loop by sampling the latent with its end wrapped around to its start. Set the latent length to 17k+5 frames (107, 158, 209, 260, 311, 362); the loop is 17k frames. Decode with MiniMax H3 Loop Decode.

pad_clips.tooltip: 17-frame clips of wrapped latent decoded on each side, so the decoder never starts or ends inside the loop.

MiniMaxH3LoopDecode.name: MiniMaxH3LoopDecode
MiniMaxH3LoopDecode.description: Decode a MiniMax H3 Loop latent with wrapped context on both sides and return exactly one loop of frames and audio.

pdd_file.tooltip: PDD Acc file from models/pdd_acc — the original alibaba-pai release or a converted ComfyUI copy, both load. Pair FL2VA with an fl2va UNET, Ref2VA with ref2va.

nfe.tooltip: Model evaluations (sampler steps). 8 = trained block size 4. 4 regroups two blocks per step (faster, official); 6 uses the non-uniform default partition 8,8,4,4,4,4. Higher step counts are OFF the training envelope and render as noise.

lora_strength.tooltip: Trunk LoRA strength. Trained at 1.0. 0.0 = baked-trunk mode: skip trunk patching entirely for a checkpoint pre-merged with bake_pdd_trunk.py (heads still apply).

head_strength.tooltip: PDD head blend: native + s*(pdd - native). 1.0 = trained path (native head not evaluated).

on_off_grid.tooltip: What to do when the model is evaluated at a sigma that is not a trained block boundary (wrong sampler/scheduler).

partition.tooltip: Custom block sizes in fine steps, comma-separated, summing to 32 (e.g. '8,8,4,4,4,4' = 6 steps, or '8,4,4,4,4,4,4' = 7). Overrides nfe. Only sizes 4 and 8 are accepted — the trained envelope; other sizes render as noise and are rejected.

enabled.tooltip: False = full bypass: the input model and bypass_sigmas pass through untouched (nothing is loaded or patched). Wire bypass_sigmas with the schedule for the un-distilled model.

bypass_sigmas.tooltip: Returned as the sigmas output when enabled=False (e.g. a BasicScheduler for the base model). Ignored when enabled.

partition_check.tooltip: fl2va and ref2va share identical key sets, so an FL2VA file on a ref2va UNET (or vice versa) applies cleanly and renders silently wrong. The loaded model's trunk is identified from its final_layer.video_out fingerprint; a confident mismatch errors. 'warn' continues anyway (deliberate cross-trunk experiments). 'off' = disable the model-type analysis entirely: the fingerprint check never runs, so nothing errors or warns about a mispairing.

MiniMaxH3PDDAccApply.name: MiniMaxH3PDDAccApply
MiniMaxH3PDDAccApply.description: Applies a MiniMax-H3 PDD Acc LoRA (alibaba-pai): trunk LoRA (converted to ComfyUI naming if needed) + per-step fused final-layer head bank. Wire the sigmas output to SamplerCustomAdvanced and sample with euler, CFG 1.0, SigmaShift 12/3. Remove other distill LoRAs (turbo) and cache nodes.

denoise.tooltip: Keep only the last round(steps*denoise) blocks (v2v-style partial denoise on the trained grid).

partition.tooltip: Custom block sizes summing to 32, overrides nfe — must match the Apply node's partition.

MiniMaxH3PDDAccScheduler.name: MiniMaxH3PDDAccScheduler
MiniMaxH3PDDAccScheduler.description: Trained PDD block-boundary sigmas (shift 12 grid). The Apply node's sigmas output is the same thing at denoise 1.0 — use this one for partial-denoise or split-sigma workflows. nfe must match the Apply node.

length.tooltip: Frame count at 24 fps, (124 = ~5s, trained range is ~124-362)

ref_image_size.tooltip: Reference image sizing. 'match' scales each ref (down only, keeping aspect) to the generation's pixel area; 'max' uses the reference pipeline's 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity. blocks_to_swap.tooltip:
Number of transformer blocks to swap between devices for VRAM optimization.
• 0: Disabled (default)
• 3B model: 0-32 blocks
• 7B model: 0-36 blocks

Requires offload_device to be set and different from device.
Not available on macOS (unified memory architecture).

swap_io_components.tooltip:
Offload input/output embeddings and normalization layers to reduce VRAM.
Requires offload_device to be set and different from device.
Not available on macOS (unified memory architecture).

offload_device.tooltip:
Device to offload DiT model when not actively processing.
• 'none': Keep model on inference device (default, fastest)
• 'cpu': Offload to system RAM (reduces VRAM usage)
• 'cuda:X': Offload to another GPU (good balance if available)

Required for BlockSwap (blocks_to_swap or swap_io_components).

cache_model.tooltip:
Keep DiT model loaded on offload_device between workflow runs.
Useful for batch processing to avoid repeated loading.
Requires offload_device to be set.

attention_mode.tooltip:
Attention computation backend:
• sdpa: PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention (default, stable, always available)
• flash_attn_2: Flash Attention 2 (Ampere+, requires flash-attn package)
• flash_attn_3: Flash Attention 3 (Hopper+, requires flash-attn with FA3 support)
• sageattn_2: SageAttention 2 (requires sageattention package)
• sageattn_3: SageAttention 3 (Blackwell/RTX 50xx only, requires sageattn3 package)

SDPA is recommended - stable and works everywhere.
Flash Attention and SageAttention provide speedup through optimized CUDA kernels on compatible GPUs.

torch_compile_args.tooltip:

Provides 20-40% speedup with compatible PyTorch 2.0+ and Triton installation.

encode_tiled.tooltip: Enable tiled encoding to reduce VRAM usage during the encoding phase

Encoding tile size in pixels (default: 1024).
Applied to both height and width.

SeedVR2LoadVAEModel.name: SeedVR2LoadVAEModel
SeedVR2LoadVAEModel.description:
Load and configure SeedVR2 VAE (Variational Autoencoder) for encoding/decoding video frames to/from latent space. Supports tiled processing to handle high resolutions on limited VRAM, model caching, multi-GPU offloading, and torch.compile acceleration. 

Connect to Video Upscaler node.

image.tooltip:
Input video frames as image batch.
Accepts both RGB (3-channel) and RGBA (4-channel) formats.
Output format will match input format.

dit.tooltip: DiT model configuration from SeedVR2 (Down)Load DiT Model node

vae.tooltip: VAE model configuration from SeedVR2 (Down)Load VAE Model node

seed.tooltip:
Random seed for reproducible generation (default: 42).
Same seed with same inputs produces identical output.

resolution.tooltip:
Target resolution for the shortest edge in pixels (default: 1080).
Automatically maintains aspect ratio of input.
Even values required for optimal processing.

max_resolution.tooltip:
Maximum resolution limit for any dimension (default: 0, no limit).
If any edge exceeds this after applying resolution,
both dimensions are scaled down proportionally.
Useful to prevent excessive VRAM usage on extreme aspect ratios.

batch_size.tooltip:
Number of frames processed together per batch (default: 5).
Must follow pattern 4n+1: 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, ...

• Higher values: Better temporal consistency and faster processing
• Lower values: Reduced VRAM usage

Ideally match to shot length for best quality.

uniform_batch_size.tooltip:
Pad final batch to match batch_size (default: False).
Prevents temporal artifacts caused by small final batch.
Add extra compute but recommended for optimal quality.

color_correction.tooltip:
Corrects color shifts in upscaled output to match original input (default: lab).
The upscaling process may alter colors; this applies color grading to restore them.

• lab: Perceptual color matching with detail preservation (recommended)
• wavelet: Frequency-based natural colors, preserves fine details
• wavelet_adaptive: Wavelet base with targeted saturation correction
• hsv: Hue-conditional saturation matching
• adain: Statistical style transfer approach
• none: No color correction applied

temporal_overlap.tooltip:
Overlapping frames between consecutive batches (default: 0, disabled).
Improves temporal consistency across batch boundaries through blending.
Values 1-4 work well for most content.

prepend_frames.tooltip:
Number of frames to prepend (reversed from start) before processing (default: 0).
Helps reduce artifacts at video beginning.
Prepended frames are automatically removed from final output.

input_noise_scale.tooltip:
Input noise injection scale (default: 0.0, disabled).
Adds controlled variation to input images before encoding.
Range: 0.0 (no noise) to 1.0 (maximum noise).
Can help with certain types of artifacts.

latent_noise_scale.tooltip:
Latent space noise injection scale (default: 0.0, disabled).
Adds controlled variation during the diffusion process.
Range: 0.0 (no noise) to 1.0 (maximum noise).
Can soften details if input_noise_scale doesn't help.

offload_device.tooltip:
Device for storing intermediate tensors between processing phases (default: cpu).
• 'none': Keep all tensors on inference device (fastest but highest VRAM usage)
• 'cpu': Offload to system RAM (recommended for long videos, slower transfers)
• 'cuda:X': Offload to another GPU (good balance if available, faster than CPU)

enable_debug.tooltip:
Enable detailed debug logging (default: False).
Shows memory usage, timing information, and processing details.
Useful for troubleshooting errors and performance issues.

output_tooltips: Upscaled video frames with color correction applied. Format (RGB/RGBA) matches input. Range [0, 1] normalized for ComfyUI compatibility.

Requires DiT and VAE model configurations.

ValisKinetogram.name: ValisKinetogram
ValisKinetogram.description: The thing is made of the same dots as the field, and you see it only because its dots move together while the field is live TV static (fresh dots every frame). Pause on any frame and it is gone. 'flow' moves every dot with the footage's own motion (connect the clip; without it, the mask's own movement), so limbs carry their own dots and dots keep renewing inside; 'follow' slides one rigid texture along with the mask; drift keeps a still thing visible. Chain: connect the last kinetogram as the field to give each thing its own motion.

on.tooltip: hits: lane name(s) to listen to, comma separated: a score event (kick, impact...), a music band (kick, snare, hat, beat, downbeat, onset), a sheet-music lane (melody, ins, note, bass, chord, bar), a syllable lane, or any name from your cue sheet

by.tooltip: a held amount: a curve (loud, bright, low, or a cue-sheet ramp) or a lane's envelope

params.tooltip: the effect's own settings as JSON, e.g. {"mode": "burn", "era": "daguerreotype"}

start.tooltip: where the loop starts on the cues (s)

warmup.tooltip: seconds played before frame 0 so trails, echoes and other effect memory are already there (-1 = the whole loop once: exact for anything that forgets within one loop; 0 = only the seal)

seal.tooltip: frames over which whatever still differs between the two passes (frost that only grows, a drift) is faded into the next pass

other.tooltip: clip 'b' (looped to the same length for you)

subject.tooltip: mask 'subject', tracked on the loop itself

gif_width.tooltip: GIF and WebP width in px, never wider than the clip (0 = full size); the MP4 is always full size

dither.tooltip: bayer: an ordered pattern that holds still from frame to frame (error diffusion crawls)

mp4_repeats.tooltip: write the loop this many times into the MP4 (for players and feeds that don't loop)

thickness.tooltip: how far in from the edge the shape reaches full height, as a share of the frame's short side (thin limbs stay thinner)

edge.tooltip: depth at the silhouette edge: how far the whole thing stands off the field (0 = it grows out of the field)

temporal.tooltip: carry some of the last frame's depth: steadier, but fast moves leave trails

relief.tooltip: a depth map of the same clip (white = near), e.g. Depth Anything 3

color.tooltip: rgb = every dot a random colour; rgb 8 = the eight corners of RGB; tv = snow with colour blotches; palette = the palette below

charset.tooltip: for look = ascii; light to dense, chosen by the noise

ValisStatic.name: ValisStatic
ValisStatic.description: What the static is made of, for Valis Stereogram and Valis Kinetogram. look: square dots, halftone dots or characters (the Valis v1 ASCII sets, a 10 PRINT maze, katakana...). noise: the grain, named like the colours of noise in sound: white is even TV snow, pink and brown clump into soft blobs (harder to fuse), blue and violet are fine and even with no clumps (easiest to fuse). color: black and white, grey, random RGB, 8-colour RGB, colour-TV static or a palette (the v1 palettes). Cells are copied whole, so a character is never cut.

period.tooltip: the stereogram's period, px (0 = read it from the frames)

window.tooltip: matching window, px: about three times the dot size

bitrate_mbps.tooltip: a hard cap, as a platform's transcode has

depth.tooltip: the depth that was hidden, for the score

ValisStereoDecode.name: ValisStereoDecode
ValisStereoDecode.description: Reads the hidden depth back out of stereogram frames: what a fusing viewer's eyes get. With codec on, the frames go through an H.264 encode at the bitrate you set first, so you see what survives an upload. Connect the depth you hid to get a score.

depth.tooltip: white = near; a MASK-made depth, Depth Anything 3, a body mesh render...

period.tooltip: repeat distance of the field, px (0 = width / 9). Keep it under your eye spacing on the screen it plays on

strength.tooltip: the deepest depth, as a share of the period (more = deeper but harder to fuse)

kind.tooltip: the dots when no pattern is connected: black and white, grey TV snow, or colour (colour detail is the first thing a codec drops)

dot_size.tooltip: px; bigger dots survive upload compression better (6 at 1080p)

refresh_every.tooltip: new dots every N frames: 1 = TV snow, 2 = half the bits, 0 = the same dots throughout (cheapest to upload, but a moving thing shows as copies across the frame)

drift.tooltip: slide the dots down (px per frame); keeps the depth, adds flow

static.tooltip: what the dots are (Valis Static: halftone, ASCII, noise colours, RGB, palettes); replaces kind and dot_size

pattern.tooltip: any picture or clip as the dots (Valis Stereo Pattern, a render)

frame_offset.tooltip: the first frame's place in a longer video rendered in pieces: the dots carry on across the cut

ValisStereogram.name: ValisStereogram
ValisStereogram.description: The hidden picture: the depth becomes repeat distances in a field of dots. Free-view it (relax your eyes through the screen for parallel, cross them for cross) until the two guide dots become three, and the thing stands out of the field. Fresh dots every frame (the default) look like TV snow, as in Black Is Good. Generated dots are drawn on their own grid, so no dot is cut or stretched by the hidden thing: a still frame shows nothing to anyone not fusing, and the picture survives uploads (1080p, 6 px dots, H.264 capped at 3 Mb/s: the hidden dancers still matched 0.87 in Valis Stereo Decode). Held dots (refresh 0) show a moving thing as copies repeating across the frame.

pregrade.tooltip: grade the reference to the take's light (Lab transfer)

auto_flip.tooltip: flip the reference if its key light is on the other side

swapped_mask.tooltip: the subject in the swapped frames: grade only that and keep the swapped background (whole-person swaps)

fade.tooltip: seconds of fade in and out

ValisTitleCard.name: ValisTitleCard
ValisTitleCard.display_name: Valis Title Card (a title over black, fading)

keep.tooltip: frames of the hold to keep (6 = a quarter second at 24 fps)

threshold.tooltip: mean difference (0-255 grey) below which a frame counts as the same still

min_frames.tooltip: never cut the shot shorter than this

ValisTrimHold.name: ValisTrimHold
ValisTrimHold.display_name: Valis Trim Hold (cut a frozen end)

audio.tooltip: the take's voice (or a ChatterboxVC conversion of it)

mode.tooltip: reveal: whip to where the pan ends. return: whip out and back to the start

speed.tooltip: peak speed, x real time. 0 = automatic (fast enough for a smear of `smear` x the width)

smear.tooltip: with speed 0: the peak motion blur, as a fraction of the frame width

shutter.tooltip: exposure per frame as a fraction of the frame interval (0.5 = a 180 degree shutter)

ValisWhipPan.name: ValisWhipPan
ValisWhipPan.display_name: Valis Whip Pan (speed-ramp a real pan into a whip)

duration.tooltip: Duration in seconds, or 0 for unlimited duration

strict_duration.tooltip: If True, when the specified duration is not possible, an error will be raised.

ref_pad_image.tooltip: Fills the padding frames of the image conditioning with this image instead of gray, anchoring identity without pinning frames (SVI-style anti-drift padding, used by models such as ID-V2V).

mode.tooltip: full: generates melody and chords; melody: generates melody only, recommended for covers.

penalty_window.tooltip: Number of recent ABC tokens used to penalize repetition.

YuE2GenerateABC.name: YuE2GenerateABC
YuE2GenerateABC.description: Generates the ABC notation of a song from style and lyrics. Connect abc to YuE2 Generate Music node.

abc.tooltip: Connect the ABC generator or supply an edited score. Leave empty to use off mode automatically.

mode.tooltip: full: generates melody and chords; melody: generates melody only, recommended for covers.

max_duration.tooltip: Maximum duration in seconds. Automatically reduced for long prompts; generation can stop earlier.

cfg_scale.tooltip: Autoregressive guidance for style and lyrics. 1.0 disables CFG, matching the ABC workflow. Use 1.01 to match the original off-mode guidance.

YuE2GenerateMusic.name: YuE2GenerateMusic
YuE2GenerateMusic.description: Generates music tokens and acoustic conditioning from style, lyrics, and an ABC notation. Provide the generated seconds to the Empty YuE2 Latent Audio node. An empty ABC input ignores the selected mode.
